blocks.text: Limited companies play a crucial role in the economy, providing a structure for businesses to operate while limiting the risk for their owners.

blocks.markdown: Limited companies are categorized into two main types: private limited companies (Ltd) and public limited companies (PLC). The key difference lies in how shares are issued and traded. Private companies cannot sell shares to the public, while public companies can.

blocks.title: Private vs Public Limited Companies
blocks.text: Private limited companies (Ltd) restrict the transfer of shares and have a maximum number of shareholders, while public limited companies (PLC) can sell shares to the general public and have no limit on shareholders.

blocks.markdown: In limited companies, the concept of limited liability is significant. This means that the owners (shareholders) are only liable for the company's debts up to the amount they invested in shares. If the company fails, personal assets of shareholders are protected.

blocks.title: Understanding Limited Liability
blocks.text: Limited liability protects shareholders' personal assets, ensuring they are not responsible for the company's debts beyond their investment.

blocks.title: Formation of a Limited Company
blocks.prompt: How is a limited company formed in Nigeria?

steps.text: Step 1: Draft the Memorandum of Association, which outlines the company's name, objectives, and capital.
Step 2: Prepare the Articles of Association, detailing the rules for the company's internal management.

blocks.answer: A limited company in Nigeria is formed by submitting the Memorandum and Articles of Association to the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) along with the necessary fees.

blocks.markdown: Shares and debentures are vital components of limited companies. Shares represent ownership in the company, while debentures are a form of long-term debt that the company must repay with interest.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember to distinguish between shares and debentures in your answers, as they serve different purposes in a company’s financial structure.

points: Limited companies can be private (Ltd) or public (PLC), with distinct rules regarding share issuance.
Limited liability protects shareholders from personal loss beyond their investment in shares.
